FROMGIT: dt: thermal: tsens: Document the fallback DT property for v2 of TSENS IP We want to create common code for v2 of the TSENS IP block that is used in a large number of Qualcomm SoCs. "qcom,tsens-v2" should be able to handle most of the common functionality start with a common get_temp() function. It is also necessary to split out the memory regions for the TM and SROT register banks because their offsets are not constant across SoC families. Signed-off-by: Amit Kucheria <amit.kucheria@linaro.org> Reviewed-by: Rob Herring <robh@kernel.org> Reviewed-by: Bjorn Andersson <bjorn.andersson@linaro.org> Tested-by: Matthias Kaehlcke <mka@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Matthias Kaehlcke <mka@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Signed-off-by: Eduardo Valentin <edubezval@gmail.com> (cherry picked from commit 4ce6dcfd0d38169d9067c768fcce8e0d49f60fac git://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/evalenti/linux-soc-thermal.git next) BUG=b:111128512 TEST=see CL:1129362 Change-Id: I3537fbb7b638a13b33b458e8f4b03fe232722118 Signed-off-by: Matthias Kaehlcke <mka@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1129361 Reviewed-by: Stephen Boyd <swboyd@chromium.org>

FROMGIT: thermal: tsens: Add support to split up register address space into two There are two banks of registers for v2 TSENS IPs: SROT and TM. On older SoCs these were contiguous, leading to DTs mapping them as one register address space of size 0x2000. In newer SoCs, these two banks are not contiguous anymore. Add logic to init_common() to differentiate between old and new DTs and adjust associated offsets for the TM register bank so that the old DTs will continue to function correctly. Signed-off-by: Amit Kucheria <amit.kucheria@linaro.org> Reviewed-by: Bjorn Andersson <bjorn.andersson@linaro.org> Tested-by: Matthias Kaehlcke <mka@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Matthias Kaehlcke <mka@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Signed-off-by: Eduardo Valentin <edubezval@gmail.com> (cherry picked from commit 5b1283984fa39933e094d237387ad8fd39527fc1 git://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/evalenti/linux-soc-thermal.git next) BUG=b:111128512 TEST=see CL:1129362 Change-Id: Ibcea1eb96654eec1f0e64250570622907f4424e4 Signed-off-by: Matthias Kaehlcke <mka@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1129217 Reviewed-by: Stephen Boyd <swboyd@chromium.org>

stats_manager: Avoid losing data In the case of multiple StatsManager, we might get data clobbered. That's particularly bad on long-running tests. This CL introduces two methods to make sure output files are unique in a directory. (1) on init, the user can supply a StatsManagerID (smid) that will be prepended to all output files. E.g. if the smid is 'ec' the summary will be stored at ec_summary.txt (2) should that fail because multiple StatsManagers are using the same smid supplied (or none were supplied) a simple file rotation is done where an integer suffix keeps getting incremented until the filename is unique. E.g. if summary.txt already exists, then summary1.txt will be created. This is not threadsafe at all so the user still have to use some caution to avoid clobbering their own data. stats_manager: accept_nan support This CL introduces a flag to StatsManager that allows for 'NaN' values to be recorded inside StatsManager. Also adds necessary tests for that behavior. UPSTREAM: security/tpm/tspi: Set return type of tcpa_log_add_table_entry as void Change f849972 (security/vboot: Enable TCPA log extension) enabled support for adding TCPA log to CBMEM. However, if CBMEM is not online, this function doesn't do anything and returns early. This condition is not really a valid error condition as it depends on when the call to tcpa_log_add_table_entry is made. Since tcpa_log_add_table_entry returns -1 when cbmem is not online, tpm_extend_pcr prints an error message with prefix "ERROR:". This can confuse any scripts trying to catch errors in boot flow. This CL makes the following changes: 1. Removes the print in tpm_extend_pcr since tcpa_log_add_table_entry already prints out appropriate ERROR messages in case of failure to add log entry. 2. Since the return value of tcpa_log_add_table_entry is not used anymore, return type for tcpa_log_add_table_entry is changed to void. Allocate GID for ext4 resgid Allocating GID 20119 for access to ext4 reserved space. Currently, this GID is allocated only for Android's reserved disk GID (https://android.googlesource.com/platform/system/core/+/1fefb9f1294d3e270f1711f41e7c77a61213742b/libcutils/include/private/android_filesystem_config.h#128). BUG=b:111529716 TEST=Tested with https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromiumos/overlays/chromiumos-overlay/+/1145150. emerge arc-base, mount_gpt_image, and cat /tmp/m/etc/group shows "android-reserved-disk:!:20119:" Change-Id: Ibeddc48c8a8d53f1497a7e5476ca1b763f8c01c9 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1145151 Commit-Ready: Risan <risan@chromium.org> Tested-by: Risan <risan@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Yusuke Sato <yusukes@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Luis Hector Chavez <lhchavez@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org>

Add Android's Reserved GID to resgid Android added GID 1065 to resgid: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/system/core/+/1fefb9f1294d3e270f1711f41e7c77a61213742b/libcutils/include/private/android_filesystem_config.h#128 We want to add that GID to ChromeOS' ext4 resgid, as elaborated in http://go/arc++:reserved-space. With current mapping, adding Android's GID 1065 to ChromeOS's ext4 resgid means adding GID 1065 + shift (655360). However, ext4 resgid is unfortunately still a 16-bit integer (this is based on observation. The code is probably: https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromiumos/third_party/kernel/+/20b3692ddbf17eda938a899c387d941a2743edfc/fs/ext4/ext4.h#1170). Hence, adding 1065 + 655360 is interpreted as adding GID 1065 (because of modulo 65536). Hence, we need to map the 1065 to a special GID that is not used in ChromeOS yet that is less than 2^16=65536. In this case, we are assigning 1065 to 20119, which is a GID in 20100-29999 range that can be allocated for this purpose. BUG=b:111529716 TEST=Restarted device and GID=20119 is in ext4 resgid (through dumpe2fs). And also tested that after Android reserved gid is added in resgid (which is container's GID=1065), exhausting disk space by a non-system Android app should not crash the container. CQ-DEPEND=CL:1145151 Change-Id: I2b61f5213f6872e50d8d09fd40b605f9a6a7446a Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1143175 Commit-Ready: Risan <risan@chromium.org> Tested-by: Risan <risan@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Yusuke Sato <yusukes@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Luis Hector Chavez <lhchavez@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org>

Simplify and fix destroy_context() Before this CL, destroy_context() walked the context table list twice: once to find the context with the right handle, once to find the previous handle. Not only it was inefficient, it also created cycles in the list if somehow to contexts with duplicate handles were inserted into the list. This CL fixes it by finding the previous context by walking the list only, and relying on the fact that if such previous context is found, then previous->next is the one to kill. drivers/storage/sdhci: Set clock if it is not already enabled On KBL platforms(poppy/soraka), it is observed that the clock control register gets reset to 0 after SD card controller is power-gated. In such cases, it is not right to rely on the previously configured clock to decide if clock control register needs to be re-programmed. This change adds a check to see if clock is currently enabled in control register and if not then it calls sdhci_set_clock even if previously configured clock value hasn't changed.
